scope_notes: Covers MMA-specific skills: hybrid stance, level change + double-leg takedown, sprawl defense, posture and ground-and-pound from top guard, and the technical stand-up. Striking mechanics reuse the boxing and kickboxing KBs; submissions/guard work reuse the BJJ KB.
source_gap_notes: Peer-reviewed MMA literature is mostly performance analysis (what wins), not technique biomechanics; technique cues come from USA Wrestling, Evolve University, Greg Jackson and Grapplearts. About 10-12 usable sources.

sources.name: UFC Performance Institute - A Cross-Sectional Performance Analysis and Projection of the UFC Athlete (2018)
sources.credibility: UFC's sports-science institute: 3,900 bouts, 167 metrics; striking volume and ground control are top win KPIs; injury patterns.

sources.name: Exploratory Systematic Review of Mixed Martial Arts: performance factors with over 20,000 athletes (Sports, MDPI 2022)
sources.credibility: 112 studies / 20,784 athletes; technical-tactical, time-motion and outcome analyses.
sources.usage_note: Background: evidence map of MMA research; not cited for a specific item.

sources.name: Miarka B et al. - Performance probabilities and outcome effects in technical-tactical factors with bout phase changes of MMA (IJPAS 2017)
sources.credibility: 1,752 UFC rounds: landed head strikes, offensive guard passes and landed takedowns were the strongest win predictors.

sources.name: Comparisons: Technical-Tactical and Time-Motion Analysis of MMA winners and losers (J Strength Cond Res 2016)
sources.credibility: Winner vs loser behaviors across rounds.
sources.usage_note: Background: winner/loser behavior data; not cited for a specific item.

sources.name: Whole-Body Mechanics of Double-Leg Attack in Elite and Non-elite Male Freestyle Wrestlers (Frontiers in Sports and Active Living 2020)
sources.credibility: Biomechanics of the double-leg attack comparing elite and non-elite wrestlers.
sources.usage_note: Background: double-leg biomechanics; specific findings not extracted (abstract not reviewed in detail).

sources.name: USA Wrestling Core Curriculum
sources.credibility: National governing body curriculum: stance, motion, level change, penetration (inside/outside step), back step.

sources.name: USA Wrestling - 7 Basic Skills Study Guide
sources.credibility: Official study guide: 5 key positions (head up, back straight, hips in, knees off the mat, toe pressure), stances, motion, level change, penetration and drills.

sources.name: Evolve University - Sprawl (wrestling basics) and MMA Defense essentials
sources.credibility: Evolve MMA world-champion coaching staff video library.

sources.name: Evolve University - Drill: Double Leg Penetration
sources.credibility: Solo/partner penetration-step drill from Evolve's wrestling coaches.

sources.name: Evolve University - Ground And Pound From Full Guard
sources.credibility: Ground-and-pound lesson from full guard (featuring former UFC champion Tyron Woodley).

sources.name: Greg Jackson - How to Posture in Someone's Guard and Deliver Strikes (Dynamic Striking)
sources.credibility: Head coach of Jackson-Wink MMA, coach of multiple UFC champions.

sources.name: Grapplearts (Stephan Kesting) - The Four Variations of the BJJ Technical Standup
sources.credibility: Long-running grappling instruction site by a BJJ black belt; technical stand-up variations.

skills.name: MMA stance (strike + takedown ready)
skills.recommended_camera: Front and side views, full body.

checkpoints.description: Hybrid stance: slightly wider and lower than boxing, knees bent, chest over the knees, hands forward and elbows in, head up - ready to strike, shoot or sprawl.
checkpoints.measurable_angle_or_rule: knee angle ~130-160 deg; head above hips (not bent at waist); elbows within ~1 fist of the torso

checkpoints.description: USA Wrestling's 5 key positions apply: head up, back straight, hips in, knees bent (off the mat), toe pressure.
checkpoints.measurable_angle_or_rule: trunk angle relatively straight (shoulder-hip line not rounded); head above shoulder line

faults.name: Upright boxing stance with crossed/narrow feet
faults.video_signs: Tall posture, narrow base; easy to take down.
faults.correction_cue: 'Lower and wider - chest over knees, hands forward.'
faults.why_it_matters: A tall narrow stance makes level changes slow and offers easy legs to the opponent.

faults.name: Bending at the waist
faults.video_signs: Head low and in front of the knees, back rounded.
faults.why_it_matters: Bending at the waist exposes the head to snap-downs, knees and uppercuts.

drills.name: Stance-and-motion shadow drill
steps: Move forward/back/laterally and circle both ways in stance.
Hold the 5 key positions while moving.
On command, level-change and return; or sprawl and return.
drills.fixes: Upright stance; bending at the waist
drills.why: USA Wrestling teaches that power = strength + mobility; moving while holding position builds the stance under motion.

drills.name: Scramble-to-stance drill (USA Wrestling)
drills.setup: One athlete starts flat; partner applies light top pressure.
steps: On the whistle, the bottom athlete fights the pressure and scrambles back to a solid stance.
Hold the 5 key positions on arrival.
Switch roles.
drills.fixes: Upright stance; bending at the waist (under fatigue)
drills.why: Returning to a strong stance from a bad position builds the habit and early-season strength (USA Wrestling).

pro_tips.tip: UFC PI data: total strikes landed is the top win-related KPI for men and women, and ground-control time is also a top factor - a stance that defends takedowns protects your striking.

skills.name: Level change and double-leg takedown
skills.recommended_camera: Side view at hip height plus front view.

checkpoints.description: Level change by dropping the hips and bending the knees vertically - not bending at the waist; head up, back straight.
checkpoints.measurable_angle_or_rule: hip height drops > ~20-30% of standing hip height while trunk angle stays < ~45 deg from vertical; head above shoulders

checkpoints.description: Penetration step: lead foot steps deep between the opponent's feet, lead knee drops toward the mat, trail leg drives through.
checkpoints.measurable_angle_or_rule: lead foot lands between/under the opponent's hips; lead knee approaches the mat

checkpoints.description: Drive up and through the opponent at about a 45-degree angle.
Set up the shot behind strikes (level change disguised by punches).
checkpoints.measurable_angle_or_rule: shot initiated within ~1 s after a punch/feint

faults.name: Bending at the waist (reaching shot)
faults.video_signs: Head drops below the hips, arms reach for legs from outside range.
faults.correction_cue: 'Drop your level with your legs - hips under you.'
faults.why_it_matters: A waist-bent shot is easily sprawled on or snapped down; USA Wrestling notes most failed shots come from poor level change.

faults.name: Shooting from too far / shallow step
faults.video_signs: Lead foot lands short of the opponent's feet; athlete lunges.
faults.correction_cue: 'Step deep - get your hips under theirs.'
faults.why_it_matters: Depth of penetration puts the attacker's hips in position to lift/drive.

faults.name: Unsetup shot
faults.video_signs: Takedown attempt from a static exchange without punches or feints.
faults.why_it_matters: Landed takedowns are a strong win predictor; set-ups raise success.

drills.name: Penetration-step progression
drills.setup: Open mat; tape line for depth; then partner.
steps: Solo: level change, step deep with lead foot, drop lead knee lightly, bring trail leg through, return to stance.
Partner (no resistance): penetrate between partner's feet, head up/back straight.
Add a jab or 1-2 before each shot.
Progress to controlled resistance and live rounds.
drills.dosage: 3 sets x 10 per side, then 3 x 2-min rounds
drills.fixes: Bending at the waist; shallow step; unsetup shot
drills.why: Grooving the level change and deep step solo before adding resistance builds the posture USA Wrestling emphasizes.

drills.name: Up-and-through level change (USA Wrestling)
drills.setup: Partner standing; attacker in stance at arm's length.
steps: Attacker assumes a low level: head up, back straight, hips in.
Penetrate and drive up and through the partner at about 45 degrees (high crotch, double and single variations).
Reset and alternate sides.
drills.fixes: Bending at the waist; shallow step
drills.why: From the USA Wrestling 7 Basic Skills guide: rehearsing the finish angle with correct posture links the level change to an effective drive.

pro_tips.tip: Inside-step penetration sets up high crotches, doubles and in-line fireman's carries; outside-step sets up singles and duck-unders.
Landed head strikes, offensive passes and landed takedowns were the strongest predictors of winning a UFC round.

checkpoints.description: On the shot, kick the legs back, drop the hips heavily onto the attacker and keep the head up.
checkpoints.measurable_angle_or_rule: hips drop and move backward; legs extend behind (knee angle > ~150 deg); head above hips

checkpoints.description: Down-block/cross-block with the hands to obstruct the path to the legs, then circle back to stance.
checkpoints.measurable_angle_or_rule: hands move down in front of the lead leg as the attacker shoots

faults.name: Late sprawl / legs not back
faults.video_signs: Hips stay over the feet; attacker reaches the legs.
faults.why_it_matters: If the legs aren't removed the attacker finishes the shot.

faults.name: Head down during sprawl
faults.video_signs: Defender looks at the mat; posture collapses.
faults.why_it_matters: Head up keeps the spine strong and the hips driving down.

drills.name: Reaction sprawl drill
steps: Defender in stance, moving.
Partner level-changes/shoots at random.
Sprawl, hips heavy, then circle back to stance or front headlock.
drills.why: Random shots train reaction time to the level change, the earliest cue of a takedown.

pro_tips.tip: Takedowns and grappling cause the longest average injury durations in UFC data, while striking causes the most injuries by frequency - drill takedown defense with control.

skills.name: Posture and ground-and-pound from top guard

checkpoints.description: Strong posture in guard: hips down and forward, spine aligned, control the opponent's biceps/arms.
checkpoints.measurable_angle_or_rule: top athlete's trunk upright-to-slightly forward; hips low (not sitting high)

checkpoints.description: Strike only when control is retained; short compact punches/elbows, then re-establish control.
checkpoints.measurable_angle_or_rule: striking hand returns to control within ~1 s; hips stay low during strikes

faults.name: Posture broken (head pulled down)
faults.video_signs: Top athlete's head is pulled down to the opponent's chest; hands posted on the mat.
faults.correction_cue: 'Posture up - hips forward, control the arms.'
faults.why_it_matters: Broken posture exposes the top athlete to sweeps, triangles and armbars.

faults.name: Wild strikes losing position
faults.video_signs: Big looping strikes that lift the hips and let the bottom fighter escape.
faults.why_it_matters: Losing base turns an advantage into a scramble.

drills.name: Posture-up in guard drill
drills.setup: Top athlete in the bottom athlete's closed guard; bottom tries to break posture (no submissions at first).
steps: Top: hips down and forward, spine aligned, control biceps.
Bottom: pull the head/arms to break posture.
Top re-postures each time; add light strikes to pads only when posture is held.
drills.fixes: Posture broken; wild strikes losing position
drills.why: Positional resistance makes posture the first priority before striking, as Greg Jackson and Evolve's lessons emphasize.

pro_tips.tip: Offensive guard passes were among the strongest win predictors in UFC rounds - posture first, then pass or strike.

checkpoints.description: Sit to one side, post one hand behind beside the hip and plant the opposite foot; free arm protects the head.
checkpoints.measurable_angle_or_rule: three points of support (post hand, planted foot, seated hip) before lifting; free wrist near the face

checkpoints.description: Lift the hips on the hand-foot post, swing the free leg back under, and stand up into a stance facing the opponent.
checkpoints.measurable_angle_or_rule: swinging leg lands behind the post hand; finish in a stance with ankle distance ~1.0-1.5x shoulder width

faults.name: Standing straight up forward toward opponent
faults.video_signs: Athlete stands by leaning forward into the opponent without a post.
faults.correction_cue: 'Post, hips up, leg back - stand up away.'
faults.why_it_matters: Standing forward without a post exposes the head and gives up a takedown/knee.

faults.name: No guarding hand
faults.video_signs: Free arm doesn't protect the face during the stand-up.
faults.why_it_matters: The stand-up is a vulnerable moment for strikes.

drills.name: Technical stand-up repetitions
drills.setup: Open mat; progress to a partner standing in front.
steps: From seated, post one hand behind and plant the opposite foot; free hand guards the face.
Lift the hips, swing the leg back, stand into stance.
Do both sides; then with a partner who pressures lightly.
drills.fixes: Standing forward into opponent; no guarding hand
drills.why: Repetition makes the safe pattern automatic so it's used under pressure.

pro_tips.tip: If a full stand-up isn't available, a three-quarter stand-up to the knee is a fallback before rising or driving forward.
